Done. `out/T2/model.safetensors` is written, one execution, no failures.

**Approach:** plain `safetensors` + `torch` slicing in `out/T2/solution.py`. The condition's advertised route for T2 — `transformers` `prune_heads` — does not exist in the pinned transformers 5.12.1 (removed from both `GPT2Model` and `GPT2Attention`; I verified). And it wouldn't have worked anyway: `from_pretrained` loads only 148 of the 160 tensors because the `h.<i>.attn.bias` mask buffers are non-persistent in v5, and this checkpoint uses flat keys, so a `save_pretrained` round-trip would drop 12 tensors and re-prefix the rest.

**The layout work:** under Conv1D `[in, out]`, `c_attn` heads are column blocks (dim 1) while `c_proj` heads are row blocks (dim 0) — opposite axes in the same module. `c_attn` is fused `[q|k|v]`, so the 64-wide hole is punched three times at offsets 0/768/1536 with segment order preserved. `attn.c_proj.bias` and `attn.bias` share the `h.<i>.attn.` prefix but must not be touched, so matching is on exact suffixes with an input-shape assertion before every slice.

**Checks that gate the write:** the three required `h.0` shapes and the 160-tensor count, plus the same shape checks on all 12 layers, all raising before `save_file`.

**Independent verification** (separate from the solution, rebuilt from the literal keep-ranges in TASK.md): same 160 keys, identical dtypes, bit-exact values on all 36 modified tensors, and bit-exact equality with the input on all 124 untouched tensors.

`out/T2/REPORT.md` records the tools, the dead `prune_heads` route, and the pitfalls.
